module_title: Resistor Combinations, Heating Effects, and Commercial Power
introduction: At this level, we learn what happens when multiple components (like bulbs or fans) are connected together, and how electrical energy is converted into heat or calculated for commercial billing.

core_concepts.title: Series Combination of Resistors
core_concepts.description:
When resistors are connected end-to-end (like a chain). 
Formula: $R_{total} = R_1 + R_2 + R_3$. 
Feature: The 'Current is the SAME' across all resistors, but the 'Voltage is DIVIDED'. 
Disadvantage: If one appliance breaks (like one bulb in fairy lights), the entire circuit breaks.

core_concepts.title: Parallel Combination of Resistors
core_concepts.description:
When one end of all resistors are joined at a common point, and the other ends at another common point. 
Formula: $1/R_{total} = 1/R_1 + 1/R_2 + 1/R_3$. 
Feature: The 'Voltage is the SAME' across all branches, but the 'Current is DIVIDED'. 
Application: 'Domestic house wiring' is always done in parallel so that turning off the TV doesn't turn off the fan.

core_concepts.title: Joule's Law of Heating
core_concepts.description:
When current flows through a wire, heat is produced due to resistance. 
Formula: $H = I^2 \times R \times t$ (Heat = Current squared $\times$ Resistance $\times$ Time). 
Application: Electric heaters, irons, toasters, and geysers use this principle. (They use 'Nichrome' wire because it has very high resistance and a high melting point).

core_concepts.title: Electric Fuse
core_concepts.description:
A safety device that protects circuits. It is always connected in 'Series' with the live wire. 
Properties: It must have 'High Resistance' and a 'LOW Melting Point'. 
Alloy: It is generally made of an alloy of 'Tin (Sn) and Lead (Pb)'.

important_entities.name: Commercial Unit of Energy
important_entities.significance: Electrical Power ($P$) = $V \times I$. Unit: Watt (W). We pay electricity bills in 'Units'. 1 Unit = 1 kWh (Kilowatt-hour) = exactly $3.6 \times 10^6 \text{ Joules}$ of energy.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: If a $10 \,\Omega$ and a $1000 \,\Omega$ resistor are connected in parallel, what is the total resistance? Rule: The total equivalent resistance in parallel is ALWAYS 'less than the smallest individual resistance' (so it will be less than $10 \,\Omega$).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: In Series, Current stays the same. In Parallel, Voltage stays the same.

exam_strategy_tips: Favorite RRB/Railway question: 'What is the filament of an electric bulb made of?' Answer: Tungsten, because it has an extremely high melting point (approx 3400°C).
